Selected work
Data dedup and tiering

12,866 clean contacts from a tangle of exports.

Four overlapping phone exports, roughly 94% duplicated between them, resolved into one deduplicated list and tiered into a ranked set of sell-targets.

  • Python
  • Union-find dedup
  • Phone normalisation
  • Arabic category decoding
12,866 Unique contacts, 7,777 tiered sell-targets Where this number comes from

The problem

A real-estate partner had years of contacts spread across several phone exports that overlapped by roughly 94%. The same person appeared repeatedly under different spellings, different number formats and different category labels, some of them in Arabic that had been mangled by the export. It was unusable as a list and far too large to clean by hand.

What it does

01

Treats a person as a cluster, not a row

Numbers are normalised to a canonical form first, then union-find groups every record that shares any number into a single identity, however many spellings of the name it arrives under.

02

Recovers the Arabic

Category and name fields that the export had mis-encoded are decoded back, so labels the owner had actually been using are preserved rather than dropped as junk.

03

Ranks what is left

Once the list is unique, contacts are tiered by how likely they are to be worth a call, producing a Hot and Warm set to work rather than an undifferentiated dump.

How it is built

ParseNormaliseUnion-findDecodeTier

Plain Python, no external service. The interesting part is the choice of union-find rather than pairwise matching: with this much overlap, transitive merges matter - A shares a number with B, B shares a different number with C, and all three are one person. Pairwise comparison misses that and leaves the duplicates behind.

What I'd watch if it were yours

Normalise before you compare

Almost every duplicate that survives a dedup pass survives because two representations of the same number were never made identical first.

Non-Latin data is where exports quietly break

If a field looks like junk, check the encoding before deciding the data is bad. A large share of it here was recoverable.

A deduplicated list is not yet a useful list

The tiering is what turned this from a clean database into something someone could actually work through in order.

The client is described here as a real-estate partner by agreement. No contact data appears on this site or in any public repository.
